title: Maximum Width of Binary Tree
statement: Return the maximum width of a binary tree, where width at a level includes the gaps between its leftmost and rightmost non-null nodes.
explanation: Use normalized positional indices in level-order traversal; the difference between the last and first index plus one is the level width.

title: Non-decreasing Array
statement: Return true if an array can become non-decreasing by modifying at most one element.
explanation: Scan adjacent inversions; on the first inversion, lower the previous value when possible, otherwise raise the current value.

title: Beautiful Arrangement II
statement: Construct a permutation of 1..n with exactly k distinct absolute differences between adjacent values.
explanation: Alternate low and high values across the first k+1 numbers, then append the remaining increasing suffix.

title: Trim a Binary Search Tree
statement: Trim a BST so every node value lies in [low, high], preserving BST order.
explanation: If a root is below low, keep only its right subtree; if above high, keep only its left subtree; otherwise trim both children.

title: Second Minimum Node In a Binary Tree
approach: Find smallest value greater than root
statement: In a special binary tree where each node has zero or two children and each parent equals the smaller child value, return the second minimum distinct value, or -1 if absent.
explanation: Search for the smallest node value greater than the root value; the tree property permits pruning nodes already greater than the current candidate.

title: Longest Continuous Increasing Subsequence
statement: Return the length of the longest contiguous strictly increasing subsequence.
explanation: Maintain the current run length and reset it whenever the next value is not greater.

title: Valid Palindrome II
statement: Return true if a string can become a palindrome after deleting at most one character.
explanation: Use two pointers; at the first mismatch, test either substring formed by skipping the left or right character.

title: Baseball Game
statement: Evaluate baseball scoring operations: integer score, C cancels the last score, D doubles it, and + sums the previous two.
explanation: Use a stack of scores and apply each operation against the current valid history.

title: Redundant Connection
statement: In an undirected graph that began as a tree with one extra edge, return the edge that creates a cycle.
explanation: Process edges in order with union-find; the first edge joining vertices already in the same set is redundant.

title: Longest Univalue Path
statement: Return the number of edges in the longest path where every node has the same value.
explanation: For each node, compute same-value downward lengths from each child, update the best with their sum, and return the longer branch.
